lots.what_it_is: Max Angus (1914-2017, Tasmanian), 'Old Cottages at Arthur Circus' (Battery Point, Hobart), watercolour, signed lower right, 24.5 x 36.5 cm per Gowans. Brick cottages with red and grey roofs and picket fences, snow on Mt Wellington behind, a figure in the lane. Cream mount, ornate gilt frame, glazed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 enlarged: the signature in dark wash in the foreground reads '..NGUS' clearly and is consistent with 'M ANGUS'; no date is visible. The researcher missed the catalogue title: Gowans calls it 'Old Cottages at Arthur Circus', a Battery Point subject. Photos 1-2: tidy, fairly tight early-period handling (cottages, fences, chimneys) rather than his loose later beach work. Paper and mount look clean, with no foxing or staining visible at 800 x 600. The frame has an ornate gilt moulding with no obvious losses in view. The back of the frame is not shown, so there is no label or provenance.
lots.condition: Looks good from the front: clean sheet, clean mount, frame sound in view. Back not photographed, and glass reflections limit detail.

lots.guide_summary: All AUD auction results (rate 1). Invaluable does not say whether priceResult includes premium. No record of this exact work. Close entries are all SOLD: AUD 600 and 800 at Colville in Hobart (2025-26, Tasmanian watercolours) and AUD 220 at Leonard Joel (2024, a 1952 work of the same size, just outside 24 months). Category-guide sales within 24 months run from AUD 200-220 in Melbourne (including a same-size 24 x 35 cm lake scene at 200) to AUD 500-1,700 in Hobart. UNSOLD last bids were AUD 100-400. No ASKING prices were found. Hobart clearly pays more than Melbourne for Angus.
lots.working: I follow the precedent used for lot 66 (another Max Angus in this sale): close same-artist, same-medium Hobart SOLD results within 24 months stand in for 'same item', since a painting is unique. Keep: lowest close SOLD within 24 months = Colville AUD 600 (10 Mar 2026); 600 / 1.198 = 500.8, round down = $500 (all-in $599). Flip: likely resale AUD 600 back through Colville in Hobart, less about 20% vendor costs (commission plus photo and insurance fees, assumed) = 480, outbound postage $0 (local delivery to Colville); 480 / 2.396 = 200.3, round down = $200. The Melbourne floor (AUD 200-220, including a same-size work) says an off-island resale would lose money at almost any hammer, so the flip only works locally. Current bid $100 (1 bid, 30/09/2026).
lots.confidence_reason: The signature is read in part ('..NGUS') and Gowans gives the title and size, so the identification is credible. The SOLD support is close, not the same work, sizes of the Colville comparables are unknown, and premium status is unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. I re-parsed the Invaluable JSON (48 hits) and every price, date and estimate matched. Relabelled: the Leonard Joel '(Lake Scene)' 200 from close to category guide (later lake subject, Melbourne market), though it matches the size. Corrected the researcher's garbled note on the 1952 work: it is from 2024-06-06, outside the 24-month window. Added the Colville 'At North Marion Bay' pass-in (2023). The researcher's identification missed the Gowans title, 'Old Cottages at Arthur Circus'.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there any label, inscription or date on the back (gallery or exhibition label, title in the artist's hand)? Any foxing, staining or mould under the mount, and is the frame sound?

lots.what_it_is: Jack Carington Smith (1908-1972, Tasmanian), 'Beach Scene', watercolour with white gouache highlights, signed and dated 'Carington Smith 67' lower left, 34.5 x 46.5 cm per Gowans. Surf breaking over brown rocks on a sandy shore, in a buff mount and slim gilt frame, glazed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 (close-up): the signature 'Carington Smith 67' in black brush or pen is clear and legible, in a fluent hand that matches his usual 'Carington Smith' plus a two-digit year. Photos 1-2: loose wet washes, white gouache for foam and quick dark calligraphic lines on the rocks, which is typical of his late 1960s coastal watercolours (Simpsons Bay and Bruny type). The sheet looks clean, with a warm line at the window edge that is likely the mount bevel or mild mat burn. The mount looks slightly toned. The back is not shown.
lots.condition: Looks sound from the front. The mount is a little toned and there may be slight mat burn at the window edge. The back is not photographed.

lots.what_it_is: Antique 18ct yellow gold five-stone diamond half-hoop ring: five graduated old-cut diamonds, claw set in a carved scroll gallery (the late Victorian to Edwardian pattern). Stamped 18CT in a cartouche. 3.2g total weight, size L approx, per Gowans, with a 2016 valuation of $3,361 (an insurance figure, not a market value).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: the '18CT' cartouche stamp inside the shank is clear. There is no maker's mark, assay office or date letter visible, so it is not British hallmarked in the usual way. It could be colonial or Australian, or the marks could be worn. Photo 1 enlarged: five graduated old-cut diamonds in a carved scroll half hoop, with the centre stone largest. All five stones appear present. The stones look small (my estimate about 0.25-0.4ct in all, which cannot be confirmed from the photos) and a bit dull. The carved gallery and claws look worn but intact. Only one angle is shown, from the side at low resolution, so chips, claw wear and the underside cannot be judged.
lots.condition: Worn antique, all stones apparently present. Claw security, chips to the diamonds and shank thickness cannot be judged from two photos.
